findings.description: The bucket is documented as public and has no explicit ACL or public access block restricting access, allowing anonymous or unauthorized access to stored objects such as customer data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects (including the customer master file) are stored unencrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled, so accidental or malicious deletion/overwrite of sensitive customer data cannot be recovered, compounding the impact of the public exposure.
A customer master data file is uploaded to a bucket (aws_s3_bucket.data) that is public and unencrypted, directly exposing sensitive customer records to unauthorized access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this financial data bucket, leaving sensitive financial records unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, leaving operational data unencrypted at rest despite versioning being enabled.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined for this bucket, so stored data science data is unencrypted at rest despite logging and versioning being configured.
